At point (120,120), all three absolutely-positioned divs overlap because their bounding boxes all contain that coordinate. When elements overlap, Chromium paints them by stacking order, and for positioned elements with `z-index`, the one with the highest `z-index` is on top. Here, `root>middle` has `z-index: 3`, higher than `root>front` (`z-index: 2`) and `root>back` (`z-index: 1`), so that’s what the viewer sees.

ANSWER: root>middle
